content.label: Overview
content.takeaway: Shelfwise manages stock and reservations, structured into six functional code groups.

nodes.title: Shelfwise Service Purpose
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Overview § text#0

content.markdown: Shelfwise is a service responsible for tracking warehouse stock and managing reservations for incoming orders.

nodes.title: Technical Details
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Overview § text#1

content.markdown: It is a deployable TypeScript service with a small admin frontend.

nodes.title: Performance
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Overview § text#2

content.markdown: At its peak, Shelfwise processes approximately 3,000 reservations per hour.

nodes.title: Codebase Structure Overview
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Overview § text#3

content.markdown: This tour organizes the code by responsibility, detailing module ownership, key files, and inter-group dependencies.

nodes.title: Code Groups
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Overview § text#4

content.markdown: The code is divided into the following groups: presentation, API and orchestration, domain services, supplier integration, persistence and external systems, and observability and error handling.

nodes.title: Purpose of this Overview
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Overview § text#5

content.markdown: This section introduces the Shelfwise service, its technical characteristics, performance, and the organizational structure of its codebase for a guided tour.

nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Dependency rules § group#0

content.label: Dependency rules
content.takeaway: Three rules ensure a readable, decoupled, and testable system structure.

nodes.title: Domain modules independent of HTTP layer
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Dependency rules § text#0

content.markdown: Domain modules (ledger, pricing rules) must not depend on the HTTP layer, ensuring they are usable in non-web contexts like scripts or tests.

nodes.title: Ledger is the sole writer to Postgres for stock
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Dependency rules § text#1

content.markdown: Only the ledger module is permitted to write stock data to Postgres. Other modules, such as the orchestrator and adapter, must interact with Postgres for stock updates through the ledger.

nodes.title: Supplier feed adapter exclusively calls supplier API
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Dependency rules § text#2

content.markdown: The supplier feed adapter is the only component allowed to make calls to the supplier API.

nodes.title: Purpose of Dependency Rules
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Dependency rules § text#3

content.markdown: These rules enforce a clear separation of concerns and maintain a structured architecture. They prevent tight coupling.

nodes.title: From the source
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Dependency rules § text#4

content.markdown: - Three rules keep the structure readable.

nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › API and orchestration § group#0

content.label: API and orchestration
content.takeaway: API handlers delegate to a reservation orchestrator that manages atomic stock reservations with a timeout.

nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › API and orchestration § shape#0
Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › API and orchestration § text#0

content.markdown: HTTP handlers in `src/api/routes.ts` are the sole entry point for requests. They validate the request body, attach a correlation ID, and delegate tasks without implementing business rules.

nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › API and orchestration § shape#1
Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › API and orchestration § text#1

content.markdown: The reservation orchestrator in `src/orders/reserve.ts` manages the entire reservation process, from initiation to completion.

nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › API and orchestration § shape#2
Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › API and orchestration § shape#3
Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › API and orchestration § shape#4
Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › API and orchestration § text#2

content.markdown: The orchestrator requests stock reservation from the stock ledger and pricing information from pricing rules. Upon successful completion of both, it publishes a `StockReserved` event to the message broker.

nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › API and orchestration § text#3

content.markdown: If the stock ledger cannot reserve the full quantity, the orchestrator rejects the entire order; partial reservations are not allowed.

nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › API and orchestration § text#4

content.markdown: Reservations not confirmed within 15 minutes are automatically released by the ledger, making the stock available again.

nodes.title: Orchestration Flow
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › API and orchestration § text#5

content.markdown: The API acts as a thin layer, delegating all business logic to the reservation orchestrator. The orchestrator ensures atomic reservations, either reserving the full quantity or rejecting the entire order. A time-based release mechanism prevents indefinite stock holding for unconfirmed reservations.

nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Domain services § group#0

content.label: Domain services
content.takeaway: Two independent domain services manage stock and pricing with strict dependencies.

nodes.title: Stock Ledger Module
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Domain services § text#0

content.markdown:
The `src/ledger/ledger.ts` module:
* Manages stock levels.
* Records all changes (reserve, release, restock) as append-only ledger entries.
* Writes entries to Postgres.
* Is the *only* module permitted to write to stock tables; other modules must request changes through it.

nodes.title: Pricing Rules Module
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Domain services § text#1

content.markdown:
The `src/pricing/rules.ts` module:
* Calculates order prices based on supplier price lists and active discounts.
* Reads price lists from Redis, where they are cached for 300 seconds.
* Does not modify stock levels.

nodes.title: Domain Module Dependencies
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Domain services § text#2

content.markdown:
Domain modules:
* Do not import anything from `src/api/` or `src/orders/`.
* Follow an inward dependency rule: API calls orchestrator, orchestrator calls domain modules.
* Depend solely on persistence and platform helpers.

nodes.title: Key Characteristics
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Domain services § text#3

content.markdown: The two domain services, stock ledger and pricing rules, are independent and have clearly defined responsibilities. They enforce strict boundaries on data access and dependencies.

nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration § group#0

content.label: Supplier integration
content.takeaway: Supplier feed adapter fetches, transforms, and records deliveries, logging unparsable data.

nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration § shape#0
Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration § text#0

content.markdown: The supplier feed adapter is located at `src/suppliers/feedAdapter.ts` and is responsible for ingesting restock information from suppliers.

nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration § shape#1
Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration § text#1

content.markdown: The adapter calls the supplier API every 10 minutes to fetch new delivery data.

nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration § shape#2
Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration § text#2

content.markdown: Each delivery received from the supplier API is converted into a restock record.

nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration § shape#3
Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration § text#3

content.markdown: The converted restock is then sent to the stock ledger for recording.

nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration § text#4

content.markdown: The adapter encapsulates knowledge of the supplier's data format, ensuring that any changes on the supplier's side are isolated to this single file.

nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration § shape#4
Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration § text#5

content.markdown: If the adapter cannot parse a delivery, it logs the error and skips the delivery. There are no retries for unparsable data, as repeated attempts would yield the same failure.

nodes.title: Process Overview
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration § text#6

content.markdown: The supplier integration process is a scheduled task that fetches, transforms, and records supplier deliveries. It handles parsing errors by logging and skipping, without retries.

nodes.title: Error Handling
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration § text#7

content.markdown: The process explicitly logs and skips unparsable deliveries, preventing infinite retries of bad data. This ensures system stability but means unparsable deliveries are not processed.

nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Persistence and external systems § group#0

content.label: Persistence and external systems
content.takeaway: Key systems for persistence and external interactions are defined.

nodes.title: Postgres: Source of Truth
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Persistence and external systems § text#0

content.markdown:
- Stores ledger entries and current stock levels.
- Is the definitive source for stock information.

nodes.title: Redis: Cache for Price Lists
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Persistence and external systems § text#1

content.markdown:
- Caches price lists.
- Data can be rebuilt from the supplier feed if lost.

nodes.title: Message Broker: Event Distribution
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Persistence and external systems § text#2

content.markdown:
- Carries `StockReserved` events to other services (e.g., fulfilment).
- Hosts the dead-letter queue.

nodes.title: Postgres Schema Changes
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Persistence and external systems § text#3

content.markdown:
- Located in `db/migrations/`.
- Executed on every deployment.

nodes.title: Supplier API: External Dependency
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Persistence and external systems § text#4

content.markdown:
- Operated by suppliers, outside Shelfwise control.
- The only external system Shelfwise calls.

nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Observability and error handling § group#0

content.label: Observability and error handling
content.takeaway: Structured logging and a specific retry policy handle API failures.

nodes.title: Structured Logging
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Observability and error handling § text#0

content.markdown:
- All modules use `src/platform/log.ts` for logging.
- Each event is logged as a single JSON line.
- Every log entry includes a correlation ID, added by HTTP handlers.

nodes.title: Request and Retry Logging
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Observability and error handling § text#1

content.markdown:
- HTTP handlers log each request.
- The retry helper logs every failed attempt.

nodes.title: Supplier API Call Retries
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Observability and error handling § text#2

content.markdown:
- The feed adapter uses `src/platform/retry.ts` for supplier API calls due to potential failures.
- The retry policy includes:
 - A maximum of 5 attempts per delivery.
 - Exponential backoff starting at 2 seconds, doubling with each failure, and capped at 60 seconds.
 - After the 5th failed attempt, the delivery is published to the `inventory.dlq` dead-letter queue on the message broker for staff review in the admin UI.

nodes.title: Retry Scope
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Observability and error handling § text#3

content.markdown:
- Retries are only for supplier calls.
- Reservations are never automatically retried; failed reservations return an error to the caller.

content.takeaway: The admin web UI is for warehouse staff, uses a REST API, and has no direct DB access.

nodes.title: Admin Web UI Location
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Client and presentation § text#0

nodes.title: Admin Web UI Users and Functions
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Client and presentation § text#1

content.markdown:
Warehouse staff utilize the admin web UI for:
* Looking up stock levels
* Placing manual holds
* Reviewing failed supplier imports

nodes.title: Admin Web UI Architecture
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Client and presentation § text#2

content.markdown: The admin web UI does not contain its own stock logic. All screens interact with the service's REST API, and the UI never directly communicates with the database.

nodes.title: Admin Web UI Users and Functions
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Client and presentation § text#4

nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Where to start reading § text#3

nodes.title: Test File Location
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Where to start reading § text#4

nodes.title: Reading Path for New Contributors
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Where to start reading § text#5

nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Known gaps § group#0

content.label: Known gaps
content.takeaway: Critical gaps exist in admin UI testing, stock consistency, and dead-letter alerts.

nodes.title: Admin UI Test Coverage
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Known gaps § text#0

content.markdown: The admin UI currently lacks automated tests.

nodes.title: Stock Consistency Under Load
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Known gaps § text#1

content.markdown: The reservation orchestrator and feed adapter can simultaneously modify product stock. The ledger uses a database row lock for consistency, but its effectiveness under peak load is unmeasured.

nodes.title: Dead-Lettered Delivery Alerts
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Known gaps § text#2

content.markdown: Dead-lettered deliveries are only discovered when the admin UI is manually checked. There is no alert mechanism for when the `inventory.dlq` begins to accumulate messages.

nodes.title: Summary of Gaps
nodes.stableKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Known gaps § text#3

content.markdown: Key gaps include a lack of automated tests for the admin UI, unmeasured stock consistency under peak load, and the absence of alerts for dead-lettered deliveries.
